answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, weighted by independent path length, no identity may audit its own recruit. The falcon holds work receipts rather than names, so the jade of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the trellis of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
